text.p: British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind on Wednesday welcomed a deal between Israel and the PLO to extend Palestinian rule to Hebron in the West Bank and said the accord was vital to unblock the Middle East peace process.

Negotiators initialled the deal behind closed doors on the border between Israel and the Gaza Strip at a late-night summit between Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat.
Israel's cabinet and the Palestinian Authority will meet separately later on Wednesday to approve the deal.

"I warmly welcome the fact that the Israelis and Palestinians have reached an agreement on redeployment of Israeli troops from Hebron," Rifkind said in a statement issued by the Foreign Office in London.
"This is an essential step in unblocking the Middle East peace process and a reward for persistence.
"King Hussein's (of Jordan) intervention was particularly helpful building on the efforts made by the U.S. and the rest of the international community," Rifkind said, adding:
"It is important to move on swiftly now to other outstanding elements of the interim agreement. The peace process must continue to move forward."

Chief Palestinian negotiator Mahmoud Abbas told Reuters the deal requires Israel to withdraw its troops from 80 percent of Hebron within 10 days and implement the first of three subsequent West Bank redeployments by March 7.

U.S. President Bill Clinton, whose special envoy Dennis Ross mediated between the two sides during months of arduous talks, hailed the deal as a contribution to a "lasting and secure Middle East peace".
